title: Hitler's Bunker Site - Quick Summary
items: **The site of Hitler's bunker is one of Berlin's most searched-for spots, and there is almost nothing to see.** The Führerbunker, where Hitler spent his final weeks and died on 30 April 1945, sat under the garden of the old Reich Chancellery. Today the spot is an ordinary residential car park with one small information board.

**Where it is.** The corner of In den Ministergärten and Gertrud-Kolmar-Straße in Mitte, right beside the **Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe** (the Holocaust Memorial) and about a 3 to 5 minute walk from Potsdamer Platz. Nearest U-Bahn: Mohrenstraße (U2) or Brandenburger Tor.

**What you can actually see.** A single bilingual information board, put up in 2006, with a diagram of the bunker layout. The bunker itself is sealed and buried. **Nothing is open or visible, and you cannot go inside.**

**Why it looks like nothing.** The plainness is deliberate. The Soviets and East Germany demolished and sealed the bunker after the war, and the spot was left unmarked on purpose so it would not turn into a shrine or a pilgrimage site.

**How to visit it thoughtfully.** It is a two-minute walk from the Holocaust Memorial, and that contrast is the point. Read the board, take it in quietly, and remember it is also a normal street where people live, not a photo backdrop.

**Pair it with real context nearby.** The Topography of Terror, the Holocaust Memorial and Bebelplatz are all within walking distance and explain this history far better than an empty car park can on its own.
